actualDiff.change: observeSnapshot now returns a per-observation materializer. Hits capture the frozen exact-payload plan; missing rows return a fresh empty factory; misses eagerly decode/validate/plan then return the fresh decoded graph. loadSnapshot immediately invokes this materializer for unchanged eager paths.

All three reads/observations still execute synchronously in Dashboard/Planner/Procurement order. Private per-root cells memoize one graph each. Private getters demand those cells. Successful demand clears materialize, retaining only that root's value.
Clarifies shared memo budget and additional per-root capture of immutable plans evicted during admission.

retention.proof: Each root observes each of the three surfaces once. Any hit it captures belongs to the admission-start Map; misses capture decoded graphs rather than an additional plan. Thus captured old plans form a subset of one bounded initial Map. Independent admitted root writers serialize within the store.
retention.release: First successful demand sets materialize to undefined. Unused private captures remain reachable with their root until the scope/context becomes unreachable.

newTestCatalog.name: warm root Planner skips unrequested Dashboard materialization while cold admission and transactionAll retain validation
newTestCatalog.oracle: Cold Planner parses all three persisted tagged payloads and their exact total characters. Warm Planner performs zero tagged parses and zero native Dashboard parses. Eager transactionAll performs one native Dashboard parse and parses over 2 MiB more characters. Planner outputs re-encode identically; retained output mutation does not persist; all SQL rows remain unchanged.

newTestCatalog.name: new invalid unrequested SQL payloads reject before root Planner callback on cold and warm stores
newTestCatalog.oracle: Independent SQL replaces Dashboard and Procurement with malformed JSON, unsupported envelope, invalid shape and negative-version content. Both the warm instance and a new instance reject with the unchanged decoder's error before any Planner callback. Restoring bytes permits the same Planner result; final SQL rows match.

newTestCatalog.name: one root materializes a demanded sibling once while nested and current snapshots remain independent staged copies
newTestCatalog.oracle: Two nested Dashboard reads and two currentSnapshots calls in one Planner root produce exactly one native Dashboard parse. Nested and current outputs are distinct graphs, mutations do not alter siblings or the parent, Planner staged values remain visible, own undefined and -0 survive, and durable rows do not change.

newTestCatalog.name: ended root scopes reject deferred sibling access before any lazy materialization
newTestCatalog.oracle: An untouched Dashboard stays unmaterialized during a Planner root. Deferred currentSnapshots and nested Dashboard callbacks reject after root completion, before any JSON.parse or nested callback. The retained Planner snapshot remains an ordinary detached value; later SQL read is unchanged.

newTestCatalog.name: a captured Dashboard plan survives eviction while other surfaces are observed during the same admission
newTestCatalog.oracle: A reader captures its warm 2 MiB Dashboard plan before changed 2 MiB Planner and Procurement payloads force eviction. Demand after admission yields the original Dashboard bytes via one native Dashboard parse, zero tagged Dashboard parses and exactly two tagged sibling parses, preserving own undefined and -0.

newTestCatalog.name: missing sibling rows invalidate old plans and restore only after a fresh SQL observation
newTestCatalog.oracle: Deleting the warmed Dashboard SQL row makes nested/current reads inside Planner return isolated empty snapshots. A missing-row output mutation does not become another observation. Re-insertion is observed by the next root, which re-encodes the restored original bytes.

newTestCatalog.name: independent writers cannot replace an admitted sibling observation and the next root sees their commit
newTestCatalog.oracle: An admitted Planner root holds its existing write lock while Dashboard remains undemanded. An independent Dashboard writer cannot enter its callback until release. The first root sees persisted Dashboard, the second commits, and the next first-store Planner root sees the new content/version. This supplements rather than replaces existing same-version CAS tests.

modifiedProfile.name: FIN-IND-005 persistence profile isolates real SQLite decode and staged snapshot work
addedOracles: Cold Planner tagged count and characters equal the present persisted SQL rows.
Warm Planner and unchanged eager transactionAll both perform zero tagged decoding and no encode descriptor reads.
Both return fresh Planner graphs with exact byte-equivalent re-encoding.
Eager transactionAll parses at least 800000 more characters than Planner on the same representative Finance state.
Six alternating timing samples per arm are observations only; no time ratio is an assertion.
Retained Planner output mutation does not change the next read.
modifiedProfile.timingInterpretation: Original four modes remain distinct. currentSnapshots timing now includes first-demand sibling reconstruction inside that scope, while outer admission and requested Dashboard load remain excluded. Do not add overlapping timing categories.

checked: Relative imports match the intended finance-persistence-performance namespace.
Optional transactionAll is narrowed before capture and called as the existing arrow implementation; no this-dependent binding is assumed.
One-argument transaction callbacks receive contextual Snapshot typing; no new two-argument callback inference problem was found.
JSON.parse counting wrappers delegate to the original parser and restore it in finally.
Marker counting distinguishes native Dashboard materialization from tagged nested clones and undefined-path metadata.
The eviction scenario uses three individually cacheable 2 MiB values whose payload-plus-native-plan aggregate exceeds the existing bound.
Missing-row restoration uses INSERT rather than UPDATE of a deleted row.
Deferred scope promises attach rejection handlers and are released/drained in finally.
Concurrent writer promises are observed with allSettled before waiting, and the held owner is released in finally.
No existing fixture, original journey oracle, product contract or timeout was relaxed.
limitations: This is static inspection, not a TypeScript compiler result.
The parse instrumentation is process-global and is scoped/restored as in the existing serial focused test selection; concurrent execution of instrumented tests would need separate evaluation.
Timing samples establish observations only after CI execution; they are not a correctness oracle.
